routes.name: Single Permit, Highly Qualified Worker
routes.summary: Work and residence permit for skilled workers with a Belgian employer. The employer applies to the region, then you get a long stay visa D.

eligibility.education: Level 6 qualification: higher education degree, or 3 years of relevant experience in the last 7 years, or ICT manager/specialist

income.note: 2026 gross threshold for Wallonia; 42,576 EUR (80%) if under 30. Thresholds are indexed yearly and may differ by region.

steps: Employer applies to the regional employment authority
Apply for visa D at a Belgian embassy or consulate
routes.processing: Embassy says visa D takes a minimum of one week after the permit approval. Some files take longer.

routes.name: European Blue Card
routes.summary: Permit for highly paid, degree-level workers with a Belgian job offer.

eligibility.education: Higher education degree (3 years of study)

income.note: 2026 gross threshold listed by Wallonia; 55,052 EUR for juniors with under 3 years of experience. Brussels and Flanders may differ.

other: Contract of at least one year or indefinite. This came from an older Brussels page, so recheck.

routes.name: Self-Employed Professional Card and Visa D
routes.summary: Self-employed people need a professional card from the region where the business will be, then a long stay visa D from the Belgian embassy.

other: Regions set the conditions and fees for the professional card (Flanders, Brussels, Wallonia, German-speaking Community).
For the D visa bring the region's decision, proof of the contribution fee if it applies, a medical certificate and a criminal record extract under 6 months old.
After arrival, collect the card at the company counter named on the application.

steps: Apply for the professional card from the regional authority
Apply for visa D at the embassy

routes.name: Student Visa D
routes.summary: Long stay visa D for non-EU students at recognized higher education institutions. Apply at least 3 months before travel. Studying at a non-recognized private school is judged case by case.

other: Admission rules are in articles 58 and following of the 1980 Aliens Act.
Fees and document lists were not confirmed.

steps: Attend in person with documents and pay the fees

routes.name: Family reunification (visa D)
routes.summary: Spouses, registered partners and minor children can join a Belgian or a third-country national who lives legally in Belgium. Conditions depend on nationality, age, relationship and the sponsor's status. The application is usually made abroad and decided by the Immigration Office.

other: Covered family: spouse, registered partner, joint minor children, the sponsor's or partner's minor children, and unmarried disabled adult children.
Sponsor routes: Belgian national, EU or associated-country national, or a third-country national with legal residence.
Exact income, housing and fee conditions were not confirmed.

sources.label: Immigration Office: sponsor is a third country national

routes.name: Belgian Nationality for Children Born Abroad to a Belgian Parent
routes.summary: A child born abroad is Belgian if a parent was born in Belgium. Otherwise the Belgian parent must make a declaration within 5 years of birth, or before the child turns 5 if neither parent was born in Belgium.

other: Only the Belgian parent can sign the declaration.
The embassy says nationality declarations by marriage and other acquisition routes need your main legal residence in Belgium.

sources.label: Belgian embassy: being granted Belgian nationality

routes.name: Short stay in Belgium (Schengen)
routes.summary: Short stays can't exceed 90 days in any 180-day period. You need a valid visa unless you are exempt, or a residence permit that allows entry. A visa does not guarantee entry.

other: Entry follows Article 6 of the Schengen Borders Code.
Visa-free and visa-needed nationality lists were not on the pages read. Check the Belgian foreign ministry or the EU list.

routes.name: Seasonal Worker permit
routes.summary: For seasonal work in Belgium while your main home stays outside the EU. Long stay is more than 90 days and up to 150 days in 365. The employer applies to the region through the single application.

other: You must live outside the EU when the application is made.

routes.name: Working Holiday Programme
routes.summary: Young people from Australia, New Zealand, Canada, Taiwan and South Korea can do a working holiday in Belgium. Work is only to top up funds.

savings.note: Minimum funds for the first part of the stay.

other: Valid passport and return ticket or funds for one.
Clean criminal record certificate and medical certificate.
Insurance.
No earlier working holiday in Belgium.
Main purpose must be a holiday.

routes.name: Orientation year after studies
routes.summary: After finishing studies in Belgium, non-EU graduates can extend their stay up to 12 months to look for work or start a company.

other: Apply to your local authority at least 15 days before your A card expires.
Bring a valid passport, proof of a Belgian higher education degree, health insurance for Belgium and proof of adequate means.

sources.label: Immigration Office: search year after higher studies

routes.name: Long-term resident status
routes.summary: Non-EU nationals with 5 years of legal, uninterrupted residence in Belgium can get long-term resident status.

income.note: For a single person, plus 346 EUR for each dependant.

other: 5 years of legal and uninterrupted residence right before applying.
Half of the time spent on a study permit counts.
Health insurance covering Belgium.
No danger to public order or national security.

sources.label: Immigration Office: acquiring long-term resident status

routes.name: EU/EEA/Swiss free movement and residence
routes.summary: EU citizens have a right of entry and residence in Belgium. The Immigration Office has dedicated pages on this right and on family reunification for EU citizens. Detailed conditions were not on the page read.

other: Check the Immigration Office page for registration steps and means-of-existence rules.

sources.label: Immigration Office: citizens of the EU

routes.name: Acquiring Belgian nationality (declaration or naturalisation)
routes.summary: Adults 18 and over can apply by nationality declaration or by naturalisation. You need your main legal residence in Belgium. Applying doesn't guarantee approval. Belgium doesn't ask you to give up your other nationality.

other: Residence years, language and integration requirements were not on the page read.
Marriage doesn't give nationality automatically, and living in Belgium is one condition.
Check whether your home country lets you keep your nationality.

citizenship.note: The embassy says Belgian authorities don't require you to renounce your original nationality.
